correctness.rationale: The exact first-to-third order obstruction follows from covariance factorization and sign symmetry of independent centered OU paths. Isserlis pairing gives the connected two-time fourth cumulant; its two positive exponential roots uniquely determine the unordered rates, including the repeated-root boundary. Conditioning on one full OU path produces a centered Gaussian mixture with nonconstant random variance, so the finite-time fourth cumulant is strictly positive. The conditional variance quadratic form gives \(\kappa_4=6c^4\operatorname{tr}[(K_aK_b)^2]\); exponential kernel decay justifies the per-time trace limit, and the independently evaluated Fourier integral gives the rational asymptotic coefficient. The arithmetic-geometric mean inequality gives the sharp floor/equality. Actual standalone verifier passed 243 symbolic/numerical assertions; experiments do not replace the derivation.

value.rationale: The motivating physical article matches the nonreciprocal dimer to an active Ornstein–Uhlenbeck particle at the MSD level. The new sharp minimal-order obstruction/recovery theorem shows precisely which low-order observations erase its two physically distinct relaxation channels and supplies a one-lag fourth-order way to recover the split, including the degenerate equal-rate boundary. Its long-time displacement kurtosis provides a second independent observable and a sharp universal minimum when rates match. Exact rates, equalities and parameter inversion make this a concrete dynamic-identification and non-Gaussian-transport benchmark, not a generic textbook kurtosis exercise. The stated conclusions are population identities only; finite-sample performance is unproved.
